title: Finnish moth detections did not show an extra warm-species persistence deficit in the main test
abstract: We tested whether warm-affinity moths had a larger recorded persistence deficit after a new detection than after a resident detection. The main sample had 95,813 species-site-year records at 61 Finnish sites in 1996-2019. New detections followed three surveyed years with zero catch. Persistence required detection in at least two of the next three years. Persistence was 30.8% for 13,246 new detections and 93.4% for resident detections. A model with species and site-year effects and separate catch curves gave a new-minus-resident thermal slope of +1.02 percentage points per C of European species temperature index (95% interval -0.43 to +2.48). A same-species-site model with site-year and species-year effects gave -0.59 (-3.55 to +2.37). Thus neither model showed a clear extra deficit for warm-affinity species. We also prove that stable heterogeneous Poisson catch rates can create a large persistence gap at identical current catches, without any population change. This exact counterexample is not fitted to the moths. It shows why the raw gap cannot identify failed establishment. Annual trap detection, source selection, few years and score error limit ecological inference. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, checks, source hashes and an external retrieval recipe.

display.caption: Recorded persistence by current catch and thermal group, and thermal contrasts in nine models. Intervals are nominal and conditional. Sensitivity intervals are not corrected for multiple tests.
